strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clear demonstration that diffusion GRPO suffers from exponential amplification of likelihood approximation errors in policy ratio computation (Figure 1)
Practical algorithmic solution: Elegant ratio-free weighted log-likelihood formulation that reduces computational overhead by requiring only single policy likelihood approximation

Strong theoretical contributions: Rigorous connection to energy-guided discrete diffusion (Theorem 1), clear error analysis showing linear vs exponential amplification (Equations 15-16), and interesting data unlearning interpretation

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple diverse benchmarks (Sudoku, Countdown, GSM8K, MATH500, coding), detailed computational cost analysis showing elimination of SFT and 21% runtime reduction, thorough ablations
Substantial empirical improvements on planning tasks: 76.4% Sudoku (+58.8%), 51.2% Countdown (+25.4%) demonstrate real practical value
Good reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, datasets, reward functions, implementation details, and clear algorithmic presentation
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Weighted log-likelihood objectives are well-established (AWR, RAFT, rejection sampling); main contribution is applying existing techniques to diffusion models, which feels incremental

Significant theory-practice gap: Theory assumes exact likelihood; practice uses biased d1 approximation log πθ(x₀|q) ≈ Σₖ log πθ(x₀ᵏ|x₁,q'). This approximation error is not theoretically analyzed; energy-guided diffusion connection feels post-hoc

Highly task-dependent results raise generalization concerns: Dramatic variance across tasks (Sudoku +58.8%, Countdown +25.4%, GSM8K +2.6%, MATH500 +0%) with limited analysis of why method succeeds on planning but fails on math reasoning

Underexplored sampling computational overhead: Geometric mixture sampling requires multiple denoising passes per completion. Cost not quantified in efficiency comparisons (Table 2), potentially offsetting per-step gains

Unfair experimental comparisons: wd1 avoids SFT while d1 uses s1K data; d1 reproduction shows lower performance than reported in original paper (Table 7); wd1++ uses different dataset (OpenR1) making direct comparison difficult
Limited experimental scope: Only LLaDA-8B-Instruct evaluated; no testing on other dLLM architectures (SEDD, RADD), larger models, or domains beyond text-based reasoning
Incomplete analysis: Unlearning interpretation (Remark 2) lacks empirical validation beyond formulation; Table 9 weight ablation only on Sudoku; no reward function sensitivity analysis
Missing experimental comparisons: Concurrent methods mentioned but not evaluated (SEPO, SPG, d2), limiting ability to assess relative performance

Methodological choices lack full justification: β=0 setting justified only by citing other work's empirical finding; ψ=1 validated mainly on GSM8K; design choice for normalizing weights across all groups (Algorithm 1, line 6) lacks theoretical motivation

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem: The exponential amplification of likelihood approximation errors in GRPO for dLLMs is well-articulated and illustrated effectively in Figure 1
Principled mathematical derivation: The weighted log-likelihood objective is cleanly derived from reverse-KL-constrained policy optimization with proper theoretical grounding

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple benchmarks (Sudoku, Countdown, GSM8K, MATH500), detailed ablation studies, training dynamics analysis, and additional experiments demonstrate thoroughness
Computational efficiency gains: Eliminates SFT preprocessing (~2 hours) and achieves ~22% per-step runtime improvement; wd1++ reaches competitive results with 10× fewer rollouts

Interesting theoretical connections: The interpretation as energy-guided diffusion training (Section 4) and connection to negative sample unlearning provides useful intuition linking policy optimization to diffusion theory
Good presentation: Paper is generally well-written with clear motivation, organization, and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Weighted log-likelihood formulations are established in prior work (AWR, RAFT, etc.). The contribution is primarily applying this to avoid ratio computation in dLLMs, which is incremental engineering rather than a conceptual advance

Mixed empirical results severely undermine main claims: Strong improvements only on synthetic tasks (Sudoku +43%, Countdown +25%), but marginal or no gains on main math benchmarks (GSM8K +0.8%, MATH500 0% for wd1). Real improvements (44.2% MATH500) come from orthogonal wd1++ using different data/setup

Insufficient theoretical justification for negative samples: The wd1 objective's -w^- term lacks principled justification. Why this particular form? Table 9 shows λ=0.5 works empirically, but no principled reasoning provided. The 'unlearning' interpretation (Remark 2) is underdeveloped

Likelihood approximation still required: Paper claims to solve approximation issues but still requires approximating current policy using d1's biased t=1 sampling. Both accumulate approximation error; only relative (linear vs exponential) improvement claimed

Post-hoc theoretical analysis: Theorem 1 essentially restates the weighted objective in diffusion language without providing fundamental validation. Energy-guided diffusion interpretation is a consequence, not motivation. Section 4 feels like rationalization rather than justification for why wd1 is better

Overstated efficiency claims: 22% runtime improvement is moderate, not 'significantly less.' Computational cost of sampling from geometric mixture undercounted. Fair comparison difficult given d1's one-time SFT preprocessing

wd1++ conflates with main contribution: SOTA results (44.2% MATH500) attributed to wd1 but actually from wd1++, which uses intermediate steps (orthogonal idea), different data (OpenR1), and full fine-tuning. This undermines significance claims for core method
Limited model and scope coverage: Only evaluated on LLaDA-8B; no evidence of generalization to other dLLM architectures or scales. Geometric mixture sampling implementation details unclear

Hyperparameter sensitivity under-explored: Introduces ψ, λ, β with limited sensitivity analysis. Footnote 2 reveals dramatic performance variance (25.2% vs 76.4% on Sudoku at different training steps), raising questions about stability and training dynamics

Missing comparisons and justifications: SPG and d2 mentioned as concurrent work but not compared. Limited discussion of why wd1 is preferable to alternatives. Why exponential weighting over linear schemes? When do identical reward groups occur in practice?

strengths: Clear problem identification with elegant solution: Figure 1 effectively demonstrates exponential error amplification in policy ratios, and the weighted log-likelihood reformulation directly addresses this fundamental issue

Strong practical results: Substantial improvements on reasoning tasks (+58.8% Sudoku, +16% Countdown), state-of-the-art math performance (44.2% MATH500, 84.5% GSM8K with wd1++), and significant computational efficiency gains (22% faster RL, no SFT, 10× fewer rollouts)

Novel theoretical contributions: Insightful connection to energy-guided discrete diffusion sampling and data unlearning with formal proofs (Theorems 1-2), providing deeper understanding of the method beyond algorithmic novelty

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple benchmarks, thorough ablations (Figures 2, 4; Tables 4, 9), analysis of training dynamics and token efficiency, clear computational cost comparisons demonstrating practical advantages
Well-executed presentation: Clear progression from problem to solution to theory to experiments, good mathematical exposition, extensive appendix with proofs and implementation details
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Theoretical analysis assumes DCE-based likelihood approximation, but experiments use biased d1 approximation; practical implementation sets β=0, λ=1 (eliminating reference policy), deviating from theoretical derivation that includes both regularization terms

Experimental setup inconsistencies: Different training data for wd1++ (OpenR1) vs d1 baseline (s1K) confounds comparisons; asymmetric checkpoint evaluation across methods; reproduced d1 results differ substantially from reported values

Incremental algorithmic novelty: Core technique builds heavily on Advantage-Weighted Regression (Peng et al., 2019) and recent weighted likelihood work for AR models; main novelty is application to dLLMs with explicit negative sample term rather than new fundamental techniques

Limited improvements on math reasoning without wd1++: Plain wd1 shows only marginal gains on GSM8K/MATH500; substantial improvements primarily from wd1++ which leverages intermediate steps (different contribution), questioning whether base method addresses mathematical reasoning effectively

Incomplete computational cost accounting: Sampling from geometric mixture requires multiple forward passes with overhead not fully accounted for in efficiency comparisons (Section B.3); practical speedup may be less pronounced than reported
